Settlement is where the co-owners square: Settlement is where the co-owners square up shared costs for a period. It gathers everyone's expenses and stays, splits the total fairly, and works out who owes whom before the books are closed.

Each household head goes over the figure: Each household head goes over the figures and ticks off when they're happy. Everyone has to be done before the settlement can move on.

Once everyone has accepted, the settleme: Once everyone has accepted, the settlement is closed and the agreed amounts are settled up between the households.
A settlement pulls together two things f: A settlement pulls together two things for the period: the approved expenses from the Expenses page and how many nights each household stayed (from the trips planned under Plan stay). It then splits the total between the households by how many nights each stayed, and works out who pays whom.
Every household has a head, and admins a: Every household has a head, and admins act as heads too. Any member can start a settlement, but the heads are the ones who run it — only a head can approve or reject the submitted expenses, mark a review as done, and accept the final split. Each head works on their own household's figures; other households' details stay hidden until that head chooses to show them.
Regular members can open this page and f: Regular members can open this page and follow along to see how the period is shaping up, but the action buttons are reserved for the heads. Every head has to finish their review and accept the split before it can move on.
Once all the heads accept, the settlemen: Once all the heads accept, the settlement is closed and the transfers between households become final. Earlier closed settlements stay available here to look back on.

Every group pays the same share, regardl: Every group pays the same share, regardless of how much they used the property.
Each group pays in proportion to its per: Each group pays in proportion to its person-days: one person staying one night counts as one person-day, so the total grows with both the length of a stay and the number of people on it.
Example: a 2-night stay with 2 people co: Example: a 2-night stay with 2 people counts as 2 × 2 = 4 person-days.
Example: if group A stayed 30 person-day: Example: if group A stayed 30 person-days and group B 10, a 1000 kr bill splits 750 kr to A and 250 kr to B.
Each group pays according to its registe: Each group pays according to its registered ownership share of the property.
